claims.text: A Ni intermediate layer between the Cu substrate and the high-entropy-alloy coating will enhance interfacial bonding relative to direct coating deposition.
A Ni intermediate layer will improve wear resistance relative to direct deposition of the high-entropy-alloy coating on Cu.
A Cu substrate has limited natural bonding capability for high-entropy-alloy coatings.
A suitable preparation is to electroplate a 5–10 μm Ni layer onto Cu at 50–60°C.
The Ni-plated Cu should be thermally treated at 500°C for 30 minutes before deposition of the high-entropy-alloy coating.
Interdiffusion among Cu, Ni, and the high-entropy alloy will form a graded interface.
The graded Cu–Ni–high-entropy-alloy interface will minimize interfacial mismatch.
The Ni interlayer increases chemical compatibility between Cu and the high-entropy-alloy coating.
Ni-facilitated interdiffusion enhances metallurgical bonding at the coating–substrate interface.
The Ni interlayer reduces thermal-expansion mismatch and associated mechanical stresses at the interface.
Reduced interfacial mismatch and mechanical stress improve coating adhesion.
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced stress improve overall wear performance.
The Ni-interlayer sample will exhibit significantly greater adhesion strength than a directly coated Cu control.
The Ni-interlayer sample will exhibit significantly better wear resistance than a directly coated Cu control.
The expected improvements apply primarily under moderate operating conditions where interdiffusion and bonding can mitigate interfacial defects.
Performance may differ under extreme wear or thermal conditions.
